Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · School & learning

school noun

also secondary school, high school, secondary education

classical

lūdus, lūdī m.

noun, second declension

Other words

  • schola, scholae f. — a school, especially of rhetoric or philosophy; a lecture

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.102: quī cum in scholā assēdissent (Lewis & Short); Traupman 31: school (advanced), schola; Andresian p. 42

    Greek σχολή, leisure, and so leisure given to learning: a lecture, then the place where one is given (Lewis & Short). lūdus is the children’s school; schola the school of a rhetor or philosopher, and the school of Comenius and the colloquia.

  • schola superior — secondary school, high school

    also used · modern · Traupman 29, 174: high school; M-O s.v. school types: high school (schola secundāria)

    Traupman’s phrase. Morgan–Owens’s schola secundāria is also in use, but classically secundārius is second-rate, of bread and honey (Col., Plin., Suet.; Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Praeceptor sedet in cathedrā; discipulī in subselliīs; ille docet, hī discunt.

    The teacher sits in the chair, the pupils on the benches; he teaches, they learn.Comen. OP 97

See also go to school, teacher, class, village.
